summary: A 1947 60-foot wooden tower beside Route 7 in Camden County; an older Wikipedia text dates it to 1948; the tower may not be climbed and current use is unclear.

facts.design: Aermotor LS40 model fire tower (per an older Wikipedia text)
facts.status_note: An older Wikipedia text says the tower is still in good condition. TopoZone says it is unclear whether the tower is still in use.

access.note: Visitors may walk up to the tower but may not climb it (TopoZone). An older Wikipedia text says the cab is closed.

events.note: Four acres acquired for the towersite (1946-1947 entry)
A new 60-foot wooden tower was erected, per a Daily Capital News item of June 28, 1947
An older Wikipedia text gives the construction year as 1948; this conflicts with the June 1947 newspaper item
A man manning a fire tower in the Climax Springs area saw men set fires nearby and came down to put them out. The report does not name the tower; the Central page places it under Climax Springs.
Men set several fires nearby in March 1964; a magistrate fined two men from Climax Springs a total of $400

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Central page's Daily Capital News item gives a new 60-foot wooden tower erected June 28, 1947; an older Wikipedia text gives construction in 1948. The story reports both dates and does not choose between them.

sources.title: Climax Springs Fire Tower (older Wikipedia text)

notes_for_editor: No current source was found: the Wikipedia text is an undated mirror, and TopoZone says it is unclear whether the tower is in use. The Central page has a FY1957-58 steel-tower quote about Flat Rock and a June 1958 steel tower ($3,700) entry in the Climax Springs chronology. The Flat Rock page carries the same FY1957-58 quote for Flat Rock, so the 1958 entry is left out of the story and the event list. The brief's height of 18.3 m matches the 1947 wooden tower; the standing structure may be a different one, so check before trusting height_m. The 1964 report does not name the tower; the story follows the Central page's placement under Climax Springs. The Wikipedia title 'Climax_Springs_Fire_Tower' is a 404 on Wikipedia, and the Wikipedia article for Climax Springs, Missouri does not mention the tower. Wikidata (Q5133642) lists it as a fire lookout tower in Camden County with no further detail. The en-academic mirror also gives the standing tower's height as 100 feet (30 m), which conflicts with the 60-foot 1947 wooden tower; the story gives no height for the standing tower.
